13/S0.subgoal: Describe the complete view of a VR system as including the user/organism, VR hardware, and physical environment, rather than only hardware.

13/S1.subgoal: Explain how stimulation and tracking data flows connect VR hardware with the user, and what kinds of user actions may be tracked.

13/S2.subgoal: Explain why the surrounding physical environment belongs to the VR system and how the user and hardware can change or be affected by it.

13/S3.subgoal: Identify the three main categories of VR hardware: display/output, sensor/input, and computer/processing.

13/S4.subgoal: Describe the categories of hand-based VR input devices, their examples, and their advantages and limitations.

13/S5.subgoal: Describe non-hand-based VR input devices such as head tracking and eye tracking, and explain the Midas touch problem and why multimodal input is preferred.

13/S6.subgoal: Summarize the main points of this part of the lecture and preview the remaining VR hardware topics.
